title: APN - NORAD Northern Basing Infrastructure (NNBI), Nunavut
description: Advance Procurement Notice NORAD Northern Basing Infrastructure (NNBI)  Forward Operating Location Iqaluit, Nunavut (with Security Requirements) Purpose of this Advance Procurement Notice This is not a request for proposals. In the context of the major investments announced by the Government and to foster a proactive partnership with industry, DCC is issuing this Advance Procurement Notice (APN) to inform Design-Builders of an upcoming contract opportunity at Forward Operating Location Iqaluit, Nunavut. The purpose of this APN is to allow Design-Builders to assess their capacity and interest in participating, and to prepare adequately for the potential solicitation process, notably by initiating any necessary steps. This is a preliminary notice regarding a potential contract, which includes security requirements. The purpose of this APN is to allow interested Design-Builders to initiate, if required, the sponsorship process to obtain the necessary clearances or security clearances (if applicable). Please note that there is no guarantee that this contract will proceed or that security clearances will be granted within the anticipated timelines or at all as part of the sponsorship process. Description of the Project and Services The Department of National Defence (DND) is investing in infrastructure developments for the North American Aerospace Defence Command (NORAD) Modernization and Continental Defence at the Forward Operating Location Iqaluit, Nunavut.  This infrastructure investment aims to ensure that the Canadian Armed Forces (CAF) have the tools they need to achieve their security and sovereignty objectives. These improvements will enable advanced aircraft operations and quick mobilization in the North for NORAD missions.   The infrastructure requirements for the FOL Iqaluit will include the following but are not limited to:  Airfield improvements;   Hangars with aprons and taxiways;   Ammunition compounds;  Fuel facilities;   Accommodations, warehousing, planning, multi-purpose facilities, and support equipment;   Robust IT, Cyber, and Logistics infrastructure.     Preliminary rough order of magnitude (ROM) estimates for the various facility components for each locations are as follows, subject to revision: Total hangar space, ~ 7,500 m2 Fuel storage, between 500,000 and 750,000 litres Office space  500 m2 Ammunition Storage 600 m2 Accommodations 4,000 m2 Fire Hall 2,000 m2 Multi-purpose facilities 9,000 m2 Indoor storage (Total), 7,000 m2 Apron 60,000 m2 Total asphalt surface 72,000 m2 The delivery method for this infrastructure will be a Modified Design-Build (MDB) contract, with one MDB contract for the site and an estimated total contract value that may exceed $5B. This multi-year contract consists of the following sequential and/or concurrent phases and are not limited to:  Requirements validation, concept development, market analysis and planning activities.   Design Phase activities.  Construction Phase activities.   It is anticipated that the Request for Proposal (RFP) will include detailed evaluation criteria; however, these remain subject to change and will be finalized and fully described in the RFP documentation upon release. At a high level, it is expected that the RFP will assess proponents on demonstrated experience across a range of factors, including northern design and construction experience, experience delivering similar asset types (both within and outside of northern environments), and the integration of design and construction capabilities within a single team. Key personnel requirements will include demonstrated northern experience for certain roles. The evaluation of approach and methodology is expected to consider how proponents plan to successfully deliver projects in northern environments, including logistics, climate, and constructability considerations, as well as their approach to Indigenous participation based on principles of meaningful participation and mitigation of potential adverse effects. In addition to the technical evaluation, a formal interview process will be conducted to further assess team capability to successfully deliver the project in a northern environment. The terms and conditions of the contract will allow for self-performed work by the design-build team.    The infrastructure work for Iqaluit is projected to be procured in Winter/Spring 2027. This is conditional on receiving approval to proceed by DND.   The Government of Canada is committed to advancing reconciliation and fostering meaningful engagement with Indigenous Peoples. In support of these commitments, DND aims to create opportunities for Indigenous businesses and communities through meaningful subcontracting, employment, and training related to the proposed project.  To align with these objectives, the successful proponents will be required to develop an Indigenous Benefits Plan (IBP) as part of the MDB contract. The IBP will outline proposed initiatives and opportunities for Indigenous participation, including subcontracting, employment, and training activities.  Contract Award and Anticipated Security Requirements To be eligible for contract award, a Design-Builder will be required to, among other things, actively hold or obtain all required security clearance(s) prior to the date of the award, as further detailed in the solicitation documents. The anticipated security clearance level for this contract is Facility Security Clearance at the level of SECRET. Industrial Security Program Sponsorship Defence Construction Canada (DCC) is providing Design-Builders early access to the security clearance application process through sponsorship under its Industrial Security Program (ISP). Accordingly, Design-Builders that intend to submit a proposal for this project and that do not actively hold the above identified security clearance(s) should begin forthwith the security clearance application process by applying through DCC’s ISP. Under this program, DCC may, at its entire discretion, provide preliminary assistance to all the potential proponents with their respective security clearance sponsorship process. To begin the security clearance sponsorship process, please submit a sponsorship request application to DCC by following the steps identified on DCC’s website at: https://www.dcc-cdc.gc.ca/industry/security-requirements. In their sponsorship request application to DCC, design-builders are asked to quote the following information, among other things: Advance Procurement Notice (APN) number (Project number on the MERX notice); Contract number 87007; and Level of clearance requested to be sponsored for. Sponsorship Process Upon receipt, DCC will review the sponsorship request application and will communicate directly with the Design-Builders to provide assistance for the completion of the sponsorship request packages. Once DCC has determined, at its entire discretion, that a Design-Builder: has started the sponsorship process prior to the solicitation (Contract number listed on their request for sponsorship) being advertised on MERX, has  met all the material requirements of the sponsorship request package, and has submitted a proposal DCC will  send the documents to the Public Services and Procurement Canada’s (PSPC) Contract Security Program (CSP). Following receipt of the sponsorship request package, the CSP will communicate directly with the proponent regarding any further steps or actions to be undertaken or the status of the sponsorship request package processing. At such time, the proponent will need to promptly cooperate with CSP  to ensure that the process is completed as soon as possible. Quest

title: Suomenlinna C52-C53 korjaus- ja muutostöiden kokonaisurakka
description: Suomenlinna C52-C53 korjaus- ja muutostöiden kokonaisurakka Museovirasto, Suomenlinnan hoitokunta -osasto ("Hankintayksikkö") kilpailuttaa Suomenlinnan rakennusten C53 Upseerikerho ja C52 Kurtiinitalo / Bastioni Bielke korjaus- ja muutostyöt (Urakka") tämän tarjouspyynnön ja sen liitteinä olevien asiakirjojen mukaisesti. Suomenlinna on liitetty Unescon maailmanperintöluetteloon ja on valtakunnallisesti merkittävä rakennettu kulttuuriympäristö. Ympäristöministeriö on 25.1.2022 vahvistanut Uudenmaan elinkeino-, liikenne- ja ympäristökeskuksen päätöksen suojella Suomenlinna rakennusperinnön suojelemisesta annetun lain nojalla. Upseerikerhon rakennus C53 kuuluu suojeluluokituksessa luokkaan S1. Korjausten ja muutosten tulee perustua riittäviin selvityksiin kohteen historiasta, ominaispiirteistä ja kunnosta. Rakenne- ja materiaaliratkaisujen tulee soveltua rakennusten historiallisiin ominaispiirteisiin. Toimenpiteiden tulee olla säilyttäviä, palauttavia tai muuten kohteiden ominaispiirteisiin sopivia. Museoviraston toimivaltaisia suojeluasiantuntijoita kuullaan muutoksissa ja korjaustöissä tarjouspyyntöasiakirjoissa määritellyllä tavalla. Rakennus C53 on Suomen vanhin alun perin upseerikerhoksi rakennettu rakennus, jonka käyttötarkoitus on säilynyt samana. C52 Kurtiinitalo ja Bastioni Bielke ovat 1700-luvun rakennusvaiheisiin liittyviä suojeltuja rakennuksia, joissa on nykyisin pääosin asuinkäyttöä sekä C53:n poistumisjärjestelyihin liittyviä tiloja. Rakennukset omistaa Suomen valtio ja niitä hallinnoi Museoviraston Suomenlinnan hoitokunta -osasto. Urakka koskee C53 Upseerikerhon rakennusluvan mukaisten 3. vaiheen töiden toteuttamista kahdessa erikseen määritellyssä rakennusvaiheessa. C53 Upseerikerhon kolmannen vaiheen korjaus- ja muutostöiden tavoitteena on edistää rakennusluvan mukaisen kokonaisuuden toteutumista sekä parantaa rakennuksen poistumisjärjestelyjä, palo- ja henkilöturvallisuutta, painovoimaisen ilmanvaihdon toimivuutta sekä kokoontumistilakäytön edellytyksiä. Töihin sisältyy rakenne-, rakennus-, LVI- ja sähköteknisiä muutostöitä sekä urakka-alueiden pintakäsittely- ja suojaustöitä tarjouspyyntöasiakirjojen mukaisesti. Hankkeelle on myönnetty rakennuslupa LP-091-2024-04047. VAIHE 1 – Rakennusvaihe 1 käsittää vuoden 2026 aikana toteutettavat työt (alustava urakka-aika 1.10.–31.12.2026). Työt on rajattu siten, ettei Upseerikerhon juhlatilojen käyttö katkea. Rakennuksen muu käyttö ja C52:n asuinkäyttö jatkuvat urakan aikana tarjouspyyntöasiakirjoissa määritellyssä laajuudessa. Rakennusvaiheeseen 1 kuuluvat vuoden 2026 urakkavaiheen työt on merkitty suunnitelmiin ja liitteeseen 4. VAIHE 2 – Rakennusvaihe 2 käsittää rakennusluvan ja kokoontumistilakäytön edellyttämät jäljellä olevat työt. Rakennusvaiheen toteuttaminen edellyttää myöhempää käyttökatkoa, rahoituksen varmistumista ja Hankintayksikön erillistä kirjallista tilauspäätöstä. Rakennusvaiheeseen 2 kuuluvat myöhemmin toteutettavat työt on merkitty suunnitelmiin merkinnällä “ei kuulu vuoden 2026 urakkavaiheeseen / myöhempi vaihe” tai vastaavalla rajauksella. Rakennusvaiheiden tarkempi sisältö ja niiden väliset rajaukset on määritelty liitteessä 4 ”Rakennusvaiheiden 1 ja 2 urakkasisältö / vaiheistus- ja rajausliite” sekä muissa laskenta-asiakirjoissa. Tarjoajan tulee antaa erillinen tarjoushinta kummastakin rakennusvaiheesta. Osatarjouksia tai vaihtoehtoisia tarjouksia ei hyväksytä. Tarjoajan on tarjottava molemmat rakennusvaiheet. Urakkamuoto on kiinteähintainen kokonaisurakka. Lähtökohtana ovat tilaajan palkkaamillaan suunnittelijoilla teettämät suunnitelmat. Urakassa noudatetaan rakennusurakan yleisiä sopimusehtoja YSE 1998 tarjouspyyntöasiakirjoissa esitetyin täsmennyksin ja poikkeuksin. Pääurakoitsija vastaa urakkakokonaisuudesta ja toimii lainsäädännön tarkoittamana päätoteuttajana. Pääurakoitsijan tulee nimetä tarjouksessaan hankkeeseen vastaava työnjohtaja, jolla on rakennusvalvontaviranomaisen hyväksyttävissä oleva, tehtävän vaativuutta vastaava pätevyys tai vastaava luotettava selvitys kelpoisuudesta. Rakennusteknisten töiden urakoitsija toimii pääurakoitsijana ja päätoteuttajana. Pääurakoitsija voi toteuttaa talotekniset työt omana työnään tai käyttää niiden toteuttamiseen aliurakoitsijoita. Pääurakoitsijan käyttämät talotekniset aliurakoitsijat on hyväksytettävä tilaajalla ennen kyseisten töiden aloittamista. Tarjoajan tulee tutustua kaikkiin laskenta-asiakirjoihin ja huomioida tarjouksessaan tarjouspyynnön, urakkaohjelman, urakkarajaliitteen, vaiheistus- ja rajausliitteen sekä suunnitelmien mukainen vaiheistus. Urakkalaskenta-aineisto on saatavilla hankintailmoituksessa ilmoitetun linkin kautta. Aineisto on järjestetty suunnittelualojen mukaisiin alakansioihin. Tarjouspyyntöön kuuluvat kaikki linkin kautta tarjouspyynnön julkaisuhetkellä saataville asetetut urakkalaskenta-asiakirjat. Hankintamenettelyn aikana tehtävistä täsmennyksistä ilmoitetaan Tarjouspalvelu-toimittajaportaalissa. Tarjoaja vastaa siitä, että se on huomioinut tarjouksessaan kaikki määräaikaan mennessä julkaistut täsmennykset. AIKATAULU (alustava) - Kohteeseen tutustuminen 6.8.2026 klo 13.00 ja 13.8.2026 klo 13.00. Kohdekäynti on pakollinen, eli se on edellytys tarjouksen jättämiselle. Kohteen esittelyyn tulee ilmoittautua ennakolta sähköpostitse osoitteeseen laura.runolinna@museovirasto.fi tai puhelimitse numeroon +358 295 336 749. Hankintayksikkö varaa oikeuden muuttaa valittujaa päiviä perustellusta syystä ja/tai järjestää korvaavan tilaisuuden toisena ajankohtana, mikäli katsoo sen tarpeelliseksi. Kohteen esittelyn aikana ei anneta vastauksia tarjoajien esittämiin kysymyksiin, vaan kaikki kysymykset tulee esittää kirjallisesti Tarjouspalvelun kautta kysymysten esittämiselle asetettuun määräaikaan mennessä. - Lisätietokysymykset 14.8.2026 klo 15:00 mennessä - Kysymyksiin vastaaminen 19.8.2026 mennessä - Tarjousten sisäänjättö 31.8.2026 klo 17:00,

Seuls les candidats disposant des capacités économiques et financières, techniques et professionnelles suffi-santes, d’une habilitation de niveau secret (ou très secret) seront autorisés à déposer une offre. Préalablement à l’établissement des offres et afin de permettre aux candidats d’apprécier les contraintes liées à l’objet du marché, une visite des lieux devra impérativement être effectuée. title: France – Turbine generator sets – Marché portant sur la fourniture et la maintenance de 2 groupes turbo-alternateurs à combustion et du système de contrôle commande pour un nouveau moyen de production d’électricité situé en France métropolitaine
description: Le présent Avis de Marché concerne un lot comprenant 2 marchés : Marché A : Marché de fourniture de 2 groupes turbo-alternateurs à combustion et du système de contrôle-commande de la centrale. Le Marché A a pour objet les études, la conception, la fabrication, la fourniture, le transport, l'assistance au montage et la mise en service industrielle de 2 groupes turbo-alternateurs à combustion identiques, leurs auxiliaires, le système de contrôle-commande des groupes turbo alternateurs à combustion (TAC) et du Balance of Plant (BOP) et la supervision, ainsi que la formation au futur exploitant. Le site d’implantation est situé en France métropolitaine. Les caractéristiques principales des TAC sont les suivantes : ▪ Fonctionnement en cycle ouvert, ▪ Fonctionnement au bioliquide de type HVO, ▪ Puissance électrique unitaire nette d’environ 300 MWe par unité. Périmètre de fourniture pour chaque groupe turbine à combustion : ▪ Le groupe turbo-alternateur depuis l’admission d’air jusqu’à la sortie de la cheminée ; ▪ L’ensemble des systèmes auxiliaires permettant au groupe turbo-alternateur d’assurer le fonctionnement et les performances attendus ainsi que les éléments d'interface pour les raccorder au groupe turbo-alternateur ; ▪ Un skid de pompes de gavage de combustible liquide (HVO) et un skid de pompes de gavage d’eau déminéralisée ; ▪ Le Système Numérique de Contrôle-Commande (SNCC) de la centrale comprenant : - Le système de contrôle-commande de la TAC ; - Le système de contrôle-commande du BOP process et électrique ; - Le système de supervision (installé en salle de commande) ; - Les interfaces RTU avec les services externes (téléconduite, e-monitoring, etc.). Exclusions : - Le montage électromécanique des équipements sur site (hors pose de la turbine et de l'alternateur sur leurs fondations GC qui sont inclus) - La réalisation des ouvrages de génie civil, - La conception et la réalisation du BOP (stockage et distribution du combustible et de l’eau), hors skids de pompes de gavage combustible et eau déminéralisée qui sont inclus. - La réalisation du système d’évacuation d’électricité (en aval des bornes alternateurs). Marché B : Marché de maintenance des 2 groupes turbo-alternateurs à combustion et du système de contrôle-commande de la centrale objets du Marché A Le Marché B est un marché cadre pluriannuel de maintenance ayant pour objet : ▪ La fourniture et la réparation de pièces de rechange, les services de maintenance et d’assistance technique des turbines à combustion, alternateurs et leurs principaux auxiliaires, après leur mise en service industrielle dans le cadre du Marché A. ▪ Le Maintien en Conditions Opérationnelles (MCO) et Maintien en Conditions de Sécurité (MCS) du système de contrôle-commande de la centrale (TAC + BOP) après sa mise en service dans le cadre du Marché A. La description des deux marchés est également disponible au chapitre "Synthèse technique" du document "synthèse et critères techniques" disponible dans les documents liés dans le portail achat d'EDF.

The payment protection shall provide protection for the full contract performance period plus a one-year period. Except for escrow agreements and payment bonds, which provide their own protection procedures, the Contracting Officer is authorized to access funds under the payment protection when it has been alleged in writing by a supplier of labor or material that a nonpayment has occurred, and to withhold such funds pending resolution by administrative or judicial proceedings or mutual agreement of the parties. description: THIS IS A VIRTUAL INDUSTRY DAY NOTICE ONLY, NOT A SOLICITATION ANNOUNCEMENT AND SHOULD NOT BE CONSIDERED AS SUCH. The Government will not pay for any information received in response to this notice, nor will the Government compensate any respondent for any cost incurred in developing the information provided to the Government. This notice does not constitute a commitment by the Government. Any information provided in response to this market survey will be used for informational purposes only and will not be released. Vendor participation is not a promise of future business with the Government. The purpose of this notice is to conduct market research and obtain information from current Federal Supply Schedule (FSS) Federal Supply Class (FSC) Group 66 III contract holders that can provide the required instrumentation, reagents, consumables and parts as well as perform the required installation, training, preventative maintenance, service, connectivity, and remote troubleshooting under a CPRR agreement at the time of this posting. The Wilkes-Barre VA Medical Center (WBVAMC) will be pursuing a firm fixed price Cost per Patient Result Reportable (CPRR) BPA in accordance with the Statement of Work for a base year and 6, one (1) year options in the near future for automated hematology/chemistry testing instrumentation, slide maker stainers, digital imaging systems, consumables, installation, training, preventative maintenance, parts, service, connectivity and remote troubleshooting. Potential sources must demonstrate experience and knowledge of required equipment, services and capability of performing said service for each medical center laboratory. Contractors shall discuss the technical requirements and assess space available for each lab and inform of Contractor s instrumentation and technical capabilities/functionality to meet those requirements. This is an opportunity for each contractor to discuss equipment operation, technical features/capabilities, performance characteristics, maintenance requirements, data management functionality and connectivity with each laboratory specific to their requirements. Contractors shall also discuss site specifications including utilities, space requirements, and weight for each instrument model, slide maker stainers, automation line component, etc. Literature detailing the site specifications shall be provided in written or electronic format for the laboratory to retain for future reference. Prior to Industry Day potential sources shall submit: Responses shall be emailed to Christa Stine at christa.stine@va.gov; Cynthia Laemmerhirt at Cynthia.laemmerhirt@va.gov . Include the following in the email subject line: WBVAMC-Hematology/Chemistry/Potential Sources . Responses must be received by August 18, 2026-10:00 AM (EST). Business name, address, point of contact and phone number Business size, any applicable socio-economic category and SAM UEI number Information for recent/relevant projects similar in nature/size and complexity along and contract number(s), Capability statement and product literature demonstrating ability to meet all of the requirements listed The proposed instruments and test menu to meet our needs Inclusion for future software updates and maintenance Inclusion of the Water Systems and Maintenance for them Inclusion of UPS s and maintenance for them The timelines for each instrument/department (including automation) to be up and running -Installation -Validation For Instruments and Software (both middleware and auto-validation) -Training -Go Live The NAICS Code for this procurement is 334516. Industry Day will be held Thursday, August 20, 2026, from 9:00 am to 1:00 pm EST. Contractors will be provided a scheduled appointment time. Visits may include webinars, presentations and/or videos and should last no longer than 30 minutes. These sessions should include the appropriate stakeholders for each laboratory. After Industry Day is completed, we are requesting interested vendors to submit estimated pricing of what it would cost for WBVAMC to convert their current system/Equipment to your system/Equipment. Please email pricing for a Firm Fixed-Price BPA with 6 Option Years with new Equipment/testing/services. Updated Capabilities Statements/Pricing should be submitted by email to christa.stine@va.gov; Cynthia Laemmerhirt at Cynthia.laemmerhirt@va.gov by August 31, 2026-10:00am EST. Questions shall be emailed to Christa Stine at christa.stine@va.gov; Cynthia Laemmerhirt at Cynthia.laemmerhirt@va.gov . Include the following in the email subject line: WBVAMC-Hematology/Chemistry . description: In accordance with Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 4.1102 quoters are required to be registered in the System for Award Management (SAM) at the time an offer or quotation is submitted. (i) This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial items prepared in accordance with the format in Subpart 12, as supplemented with additional information included in this notice. (v) List of Contract Line Item Numbers (CLINs), items, quantities, and units of measure: See Attached SF-1449 (vi) Description of requirements for the items to be acquired: Use/rental of an existing/established firing range. See attached Statement of Work for specific requirements for an acceptable firing range. (vii) Delivery, acceptance, and FOB point are at the contractor's facility. (viii) The provision at 52.212-1, Instructions to Offerors -- Commercial applies to this acquisition. Please see addenda to the provision. (ix) The provision at 52.212-2, Evaluation -- Commercial Services applies to the solicitation. Please see addenda to the provision. The evaluation procedures to be used are as follows: Award will be made using the lowest price technically acceptable (LPTA) selection process. Award may be made on initial quotations. Therefore, each initial quote should contain the quoter's best terms from a technical and price standpoint. However, the Government reserves the right to contact quoters if it is later determined by the contracting officer to be necessary or in the government's best interests. The LPTA process will proceed as follows: 1) Quotes may be removed from consideration for, but not limited to, the following reasons: � Quotes that are not received timely � Quotes that fail to follow the instructions in FAR Provision 52.212-1 � Quotes that fail to submit ALL required documentation/provisions � Quotes that do not provide completed pricing table � Quotes that have language inconsistent with the terms and conditions set forth in the solicitation 2) Quotes will be ordered by price from lowest to highest. 3) The Government will then review Factor 1 of the lowest priced quote. If the review finds that Factor 1 of the lowest priced quote is acceptable, the Government will then evaluate Factor 2 of the lowest priced quote. If the review finds that Factor 2 of the lowest priced quote is acceptable, that quote represents the best value to the Government and the technical evaluation process stops at this point. Contingent upon a subsequent determination of price reasonableness (Factor 3) and of contractor responsibility by the Contracting Officer, an award will be made to that quoter without further consideration of any other quoters. If the lowest quote is determined not to be acceptable for any reason, then the next lowest priced quote will receive an evaluation as described above. The process will continue in order by price until a quote from a responsible contractor is determined to be acceptable and priced fairly and reasonably. 4) USING THIS PROCEDURE, THE GOVERNMENT MAY NOT EVALUATE ALL QUOTES. (e) Each Factor will be evaluated as follows: Factor 1. Technical Acceptability Technical Acceptability will be rated on an "acceptable" or "unacceptable" basis as follows: Acceptable - The quoted range meets all technical criterion stated in the Statement of Work. Unacceptable - The quoted range does not meet all technical criterion stated in the Statement of Work. Factor 2. Past Performance Past performance will be rated on an "acceptable" or "unacceptable" basis as follows: Acceptable - Based on the quoter's performance record, the Government has a reasonable expectation that the quoter will successfully perform the required effort, or the quoter's performance record is unknown. (See note below.) Unacceptable - Based on the quoter's performance record, the Government has no reasonable expectation that the quoter will be able to successfully perform the required effort Note: In the case of a quoter without a record of relevant past performance, or for whom information on past performance is not available or so sparse that no meaningful past performance rating can be reasonably assigned, the quoter may not be evaluated favorably or unfavorably on past performance. Therefore, the quoter shall be determined to have unknown past performance. In the context of acceptability/unacceptability, "unknown" shall be considered "acceptable." Note: Quoters are not required or requested to submit past performance references. The Government will use public and Government-restricted sources (e.g. CPARS) to evaluate past performance. Factor 3. Price Price will not be rated. Price analysis will be conducted to determine reasonableness. Submission Requirements - Completed Pricing schedule - Acknowledgement of Statement of Work requirements - Most recent Lead Testing results in accordance with OSHA - Applicable fill in clauses and provisions (in terms and conditions section) - Subcontractor Agreement if Applicable (x) This is not a rated Defense Priorities and Allocations System (DPAS) order. (xi) All questions must be received no later August 24, 2026 via email to the points of contact listed at 1:00 pm Eastern Time. (xii) For more information contact Delisa.Hawkins@tsa.dhs.gov. ---END OF 70T05026Q6115N005---

title: Q701--Radiation Oncology Quality Surveillance (VHA-ROQS) Program
description: 1. Description The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), Veteran Health Administration (VHA), intends to issue a solicitation for contractor support to sustain and enhance the Radiation Oncology Quality Surveillance (VHA ROQS) Program. The contractor will evaluate, update, and maintain evidence based clinical quality measures (CQMs) used to monitor and improve radiotherapy quality across VHA radiation oncology practices nationwide This acquisition supports ongoing development of CQMs, SME driven updates, decision tree logic validation, and continuous quality improvement activities. 2. Scope of Work The contractor shall provide services including but not limited to: Evaluating existing CQM measure sets and prioritizing updates based on current evidence, performance data, and national guidelines. Convening Subject Matter Expert (SME) panels to define, revise, and validate CQMs. Developing and updating scoring logic, clinical/dosimetry data elements, and decision trees used to determine Pass/Fail/Exclusion scoring. Ensuring decision tree applicability across all 41 VHA radiation oncology services and communicating any exceptions in writing. Providing ongoing stakeholder support, including monthly calls with the NROP office and structured communication with the COR. Delivering a detailed project timeline outlining tasks, milestones, and deliverables 3. Performance Objectives The contractor will: Evaluate and revise each measure set at least once every two years. Develop or update two measure sets annually. Establish expected performance rates for each CQM. Validate logic models and ensure alignment with current literature, consensus practices, and anticipated standards of care. Support VHA s quality surveillance program without influencing or formulating VHA policy (policy decisions remain solely within VHA) 4. Security Requirements Certification & Accreditation (C&A) requirements do not apply. A Security Accreditation Package is not required 5. Procurement Status This requirement is unrestricted at the pre solicitation stage. The VA will determine set aside status following completion of market research. 6. Solicitation Availability The solicitation will be posted to SAM.gov on or about: July 30,2026 No solicitation is currently available. No telephone inquiries will be accepted. 7. Point of Contact Contracting Office: Department of Veterans Affairs Email: Cassie.white@va.gov Additional Instructions: All future updates, Q&A, and amendments will be posted to SAM.gov only.

title: Transcriptomic characterization of plasma exosomes
description: The primary purpose of this acquisition is to obtain consumables and reagents essential for processing 650 plasma exosomal RNA samples for next generation sequencing. The Center for Research on Genomics and Global employs various molecular biology techniques to investigate the pathophysiology of cardiometabolic diseases and associated traits across diverse populations. This project aims to characterize the gene expression profile of plasma exosomes, which are implicated in several diseases. Plasma, a biological fluid collected via minimally invasive methods, serves as an indicator of health and disease status. Molecular analysis of plasma may further elucidate disease mechanisms and facilitate the discovery of novel biomarkers. Consumables and reagents supplied by New England Biolabs (NEB) are utilized in generating all necessary products for sequencing on the Illumina platform, the system currently available to NHGRI investigators through the core laboratory supporting this ongoing project.

title: 6515-- SomnoFlo Electronic Vaporizer Systems Brand Name or Equal
description: This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial products and commercial services prepared in accordance with the format Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO) in Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) subpart 12.202, Streamlined Procedures for Evaluation and Solicitation for Commercial Products and Commercial Services, as supplemented with additional information included in this notice. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation; quotes are being requested, and a written solicitation document will not be issued. This solicitation is issued as an RFQ. The solicitation document and incorporated provisions and clauses are those in effect through Federal Acquisition Circular 2026-01 effective date 3/13/2026. This solicitation is unrestricted. The associated North American Industrial Classification System (NAICS) code for this procurement is 334516, with a small business size standard of 1000. The FSC/PSC is 6515. VA New Jersey Health Care System s Research and Development Service located at 385 Tremont Avenue East Orange, NJ 07018-1023 is seeking to purchase SomnoFlo Electronic Vaporizer Systems Brand Name or Equal. All interested companies shall provide quotations for the following: STATEMENT OF WORK Contract Title: SomnoFlo Electronic Vaporizer Systems Brand Name or Equal Station: VA New Jersey Health Care System (VANJHCS) (STA 561) Service Line: Research and Development Service Background: VANJHCS was awarded funds for two survival surgery stations and two non-survival surgery stations by the Lab Animal Major Equipment (LAM) program, which is sponsored by VHA s Office of Research and Development (ORD). Our current survival surgery station was constructed in-house 20+ years ago and has become a subject of concern identified by safety inspections. It was not designed for the use of isoflurane during prolonged surgeries, and with our transition away from narcotics to isoflurane, the associated infrastructure needs to change as well for the safety of the staff in the Veterinary Medical Unit (VMU). The creation of four separate surgery stations requires each to have a dedicated vaporizer system to deliver the anesthetic gas (isoflurane). Currently, there is an 8-year-old system that is moved around to accommodate the need for survival and non-survival surgeries within the VMU building. This has added to the wear-and-tear on the tubing and the connectors. Therefore, we are requesting to purchase a singular dedicated system for each surgical station. This should elongate the life of the connectors and tubing and remove a level of complexity and safety that is involved when moving around compressed gases. Scope: The Research and Development Service is requesting a new requirement to purchase 4 dedicated vaporizer systems (Electronic Vaporizer Systems) to deliver anesthetic gas (isoflurane) to 4 separate surgery stations. The vaporizer system, and connected surgery stations, will be for rat and mouse surgeries and are not associated with any specific laboratory. Serves as both an anesthesia setup and vaporizer - it directly connects to the animal via the induction chamber and nose cone for both induction and animal surgery. This dual function eliminates the need to purchase an additional, standalone vaporizer set up. Utilizes room air, eliminating the need for additional oxygen tanks. Uses less anesthetic than traditional vaporizers (down to 0.05 LPM), and this significantly reduces anesthetic waste and spillover into the room and reduces possible inhalation by technicians. Salient characteristics: The system directly connects to the animal via the induction chamber and nose cone for both induction and animal surgery, eliminating the need to purchase an additional, standalone vaporizer set up. Calculates the individual required anesthesia for each animal based on the animal s weight, ensuring the animal is receiving the proper amount of anesthetic throughout the course of the procedure and greatly reducing chance of over or under anesthetizing the animal. Draws anesthetic directly from the bottle, reducing the risk of spillage and inhalation. Contains a feature that properly disposes of any waste and unused medication, ensuring very limited technician contact with isoflurane. Touchscreen control. Flow rates from 50mL/min to 1L/min Anesthetic delivery control at 0.1% intervals. Electronic sensor auto regulates gas flow. Two modes of operation, ambient air and compressed gas. Belgium – Architectural, construction, engineering and inspection services – Aanstellen van een ontwerpteam voor bouwprojecten
description: KKarus VZW is een psychiatrisch ziekenhuis en biedt passende zorg op weg naar herstel voor mensen met psychische moeilijkheden en hun omgeving. Voor de realisatie van hun zorgstrategische doelstellingen heeft Karus een infrastructureel masterplan opgesteld, waarbij de toekomstige infrastructuur de volledige uitrol van de gedefinieerde zorgstrategie mogelijk moet maken. Algemene uitgangspunten bij dit masterplan zijn : • Centralisatie van het gespecialiseerd behandelaanbod op campus Merelbeke-Melle; • Infrastructuur die bijdraagt aan de zorgstrategie; • Woon- en leefkwaliteit: healing environment in een groene omgeving; • Duurzaamheid; • Efficiënte en kwalitatieve exploitatie; • Kwalitatieve werkomgeving; • Externe synergieën; • Respect voor de culturele waarde. Karus vzw wenst in deze fase van het masterplan : De opmaak van een campusinrichtingsplan voor het volledige psychiatrisch ziekenhuis op de campus te Merelbeke-Melle, gebaseerd op het huidige infrastructureel masterplan van Karus. In dit inrichtingsplan worden de ruimtelijke organisatie, functies en circulatiestructuren integraal uitgewerkt. Het plan vertaalt de zorgvisie naar een helende, veilige en overzichtelijke leefomgeving, met aandacht voor privacy, therapie, natuurbeleving en toekomstgerichte flexibiliteit. Daarnaast worden nutsvoorzieningen, logistieke diensten en de bereikbaarheid voor hulpdiensten zorgvuldig ingepast, zodat een efficiënt, veilig en robuust functioneren van de campus wordt gegarandeerd. Gebouwen, landschap en infrastructuur worden daarbij in samenhang benaderd, met oog voor duurzaamheid en fasering. Renovatie van bestaande gebouwen De opdracht omvat de renovatie van drie bestaande gebouwen gelegen binnen de historische campus te Melle: Gebouw M50 – Sint-Jozef: bruto vloeroppervlakte van ca. 1.700 m², verdeeld over drie bouwlagen; Gebouw M9 – Jericho: bruto vloeroppervlakte van ca. 2.880 m², verdeeld over drie bouwlagen; Gebouw M12 – Oude Wasserij: bruto vloeroppervlakte van ca. 1.130 m², verdeeld over twee bouwlagen. Deze gebouwen maken deel uit van de oorspronkelijke bebouwing van het psychiatrisch ziekenhuis en dateren van het begin van de twintigste eeuw. Zij zijn reeds geruime tijd buiten gebruik. De ruwe structuur van deze gebouwen biedt mogelijkheden om nieuwe functies te herbergen, maar de bouwfysische staat vereist grondige aanpassingen. Hoewel de gebouwen niet beschermd zijn als monument, maken zij samen met de overige historische gebouwen op de site deel uit van de vastgestelde inventaris van het bouwkundig erfgoed sinds 14 september 2009. De renovatie heeft tot doel de gebouwen geschikt te maken voor de huisvesting van afdelingen voor (jong)volwassenen, met zowel dagbehandeling als residentiële behandeling. Nieuwbouw Daarnaast omvat de opdracht het ontwerp van een nieuwbouwafdeling met een bruto vloeroppervlakte van circa 3.800 m², bestemd voor zowel dagbehandeling als residentiële behandeling van kinderen en jongeren. De nieuwbouw zal worden gerealiseerd op de terreinen van Karus, gelegen buiten de historische campus, aan de overzijde van de Caritasstraat. Tot een afdeling behoren uiteraard de kamers van zorgvragers, maar ook o.a. gemeenschappelijke ruimtes, vergaderlokalen, therapieruimtes, burelen als ook terreinaanleg, omgevingswerken, vast meubilair, ... Wat uiteindelijk zal gebouwd worden is de conclusie van een iteratief en dialectisch proces tussen de bouwheer en de ontwerper. Hierbij condenseert de kruising tussen enerzijds expertise en visie m.b.t. de dienstverlening en anderzijds de expertise rond kwaliteit van ruimte en grondige kennis van materialen en technologie in een uiteindelijk plan. Aan de inschrijvers wordt de vrijheid gelaten om aan de technisch complexe opdracht zelf vorm te geven, onder andere op het vlak van het realiseren van alternatieve bouwconfiguraties, interne circulatie, materiaalkeuzes, (zorg)technische inrichting, enz. Er dient bovendien rekening gehouden te worden met tal van bijkomende factoren, zoals het langlopend onderhoud en de exploitatie, alsook overige omstandigheden/overwegingen.. Teneinde de visie op het volledige project, de conceptuele originaliteiten en de architecturale kwaliteit tussen de verschillende concepten te kunnen evalueren dient nauw overleg kunnen gepleegd te worden met de inschrijvers teneinde de meest optimale oplossing te achterhalen. De ontwerpopdracht omvat alle relevante disciplines : architectuur, stabiliteit, technieken (HVAC, sanitair, elektriciteit, liften, brandbestrijding, akoestiek, (B)EN-studie…), EPB-verslaggeving, interieurinrichting en omgevingsaanleg. De inschrijver dient daarvoor een team samen te stellen dat beschikt over alle nodige beroepskwalificaties en -ervaring in deze disciplines, en dient daarvoor ook de nodige referenties te kunnen voorleggen. Indicatief wordt er rekening gehouden met een totale bouwkost van 35.000.000 euro (excl. erelonen, excl. BTW) Dit richtbudget is gebaseerd op de huidige inzichten, welke tijdens het ontwerpproces uiteraard nog kunnen bijgestuurd worden en het bedrag is in die zin dan ook louter indicatief. Het is duidelijk dat het ontwerp van deze opdracht reeds meebepalend kan zijn voor de later uit te voeren (ver-)nieuwbouwprojecten uit het masterplan van Karus vzw, en dat er bijgevolg gestreefd dient te worden naar maximale integratie en synergie met de reeds uitgevoerde projecten. Karus vzw behoudt zich daarom expliciet het recht voor om binnen de drie jaar na sluiting van onderhavige opdracht de uitvoering van het ontwerp van één of meer latere (ver-) nieuwbouwprojecten op deze site bij de ontwerper van deze opdracht te plaatsen middels een onderhandelingsprocedure zonder voorafgaande bekendmaking, conform art. 42 §1 2° van de Wet van 17 juni 2016 inzake overheidsopdrachten. description: Request for Bids/Quotations for a 2026 Toyota Land cruiser 250 VX (Brand Name or Equal) including delivery to Nuuk, Greenland. This is a brand name or equal acquisition as outlined in FAR 52.211-6. As of Thursday, August 13, 2026, the U.S. Embassy is soliciting quotations for a 2026 Toyota Land cruiser 250 VX (Brand Name or Equal) including delivery to Nuuk, Greenland. The vehicle needs to have the following specifications: Engine type T24A-FTS � 2.4L turbocharged petrol, 4-cyl. in-line Displacement 2,393 cc Valve system 16-valve DOHC Max power 278 hp (204 kW), figure as announced at European unveil Max torque 430 Nm (316 lb-ft) Transmission 8-speed automatic (Direct Shift) Drive type Full-time 4WD Fuel type Petrol (unleaded) � no diesel particulate/AdBlue system required Note Distinct from the US i-Force Max 2.4L hybrid (326 hp/465 lb-ft) � this unit is non-hybrid Wheels & tires 18-in alloy wheels Lighting Round LED headlamps, LED DRLs and fog lamps Infotainment 12.3-in Toyota Smart Connect touchscreen, 12.3-in digital cockpit Driver assistance Toyota Safety Sense, Adaptive Cruise Control, Multi-Terrain Monitor, Panoramic View Monitor Off-road systems Crawl Control, Stabilizer Disconnect Mechanism, electronic locking rear differential Comfort Heated steering wheel, dual-zone climate, power-adjustable front seats, cooled rear console box Options 7-seat layout, sunroof The vendor is required to submit a duty- and tax-free quote including shipping to Nuuk Greenland, registration fees, and warranty details. The vehicle is required to meet or exceed EU/Danish/Greenlandic road worthiness requirements. The contract will be a firm fixed priced contract. Note: US-made vehicles and Danish/Greenlandic-made vehicles differ primarily in regulatory compliance and market preferences. US vehicles are built to meet American standards, which include specific lighting requirements such as amber turn signals and sealed-beam headlights, as well as odometers that measure in miles. In contrast, Danish/Greenlandic vehicles adhere to European Union regulations, featuring E-marked lighting with rear fog lights and metric odometers in kilometers. Additionally, European emission standards for Danish/Greenlandic cars are generally stricter, influencing engine design and fuel efficiency. Special Notice: Brand Name Haworth Furniture Solicitation Number: FA8601-26-Q-0111 Notice Type: Special (RFQ) Issuing Office: AFLCMC/PZIBA Posted Date: July 28, 2026 Response Date: August 31, 2026, 11:00 AM EDT Set-Aside: N/A Classification Code (PSC): 7110 NAICS Code: 337214 Small Business Size Standard: 1,100 Employees Description: The Air Force Life Cycle Management Center (AFLCMC/PZIBA), on behalf of Department of the Air Force at Wright Patterson Air Force Base (WPAFB), intends to award a Brand Name Only, firm-fixed-price contract for Haworth Furniture. This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial products prepared in accordance with Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation Overhaul (RFO) Part 12. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation; offers are being requested and a separate written solicitation will not be issued. This solicitation incorporates provisions and clauses in effect through the RFO (effective April 17, 2026) and the Revolutionary Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation Supplement (RDFARS) as of the date of issuance. The Department of the Air Force intends to award a firm-fixed-price contract for Haworth Furniture in accordance with the attached Statement of Work (SOW), on a Lowest Price Technically Acceptable (LPTA) basis. The Schedule of Supplies, place of performance, delivery information, and the full list of applicable provisions and clauses are set forth in the attached SF 1449 and solicitation. Award is subject to the availability of funds. The requirement is for all supplies, labor, and services necessary to complete the furniture requirement of WBAFB. This is a follow-on project that requires new workstations to be physically compatible and fully interchangeable with the existing Haworth furniture. The Government's market research indicates that Haworth products utilize proprietary physical connections, and no other manufacturer produces a compatible system that can meet the Government's essential need for a single, integrated, and reconfigurable workspace. In accordance with the Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation Overhaul, (RFO) 5.101(c)(4)(vii), the justification for restricting competition is that the proprietary Haworth physical connections and design are essential to the Government's requirement, and no other brand of systems furniture can interface with the existing setup. Therefore, this acquisition is being conducted under the authority of (RFO) 6.103-1. This is a BRAND NAME ONLY requirement. Only brand name Haworth products will be accepted. "Or Equal" products will NOT be evaluated. Standardization of Haworth is required to ensure compatibility with existing systems, eliminate duplication of training costs and maintain mission continuity. In accordance with RFO 5.201(c)(3), the approved Brand Name Justification and Approval (J&A) is attached to this posting on SAM.gov. title: Durable Medical Equipment Request for Information (RFI)
description: FEDERAL EMERGENCY MANAGEMENT AGENCY DURABLE MEDICAL EQUIPMENT REQUEST FOR INFORMATION The Department of Homeland Security (DHS), Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA), Logistics Management Division, Distribution Management Division, Supply Chain Integration Branch, seeks to identify and assess industry capabilities to provide disaster Durable Medical Equipment in support of emergency response and steady-state operations within the Continental United States (CONUS) and Outside the Continental United States (OCONUS). The information collected will be used to support contingency planning, requirements development, and operational readiness assessments related to mass sheltering operations during natural disasters, humanitarian assistance, and other emergency response scenarios. This RFI is issued solely for information gathering purposes to identify sources that can provide support for the Supply Chain Integration Branch. In accordance with FAR 15.101(e), RFIs may be used when the Government wants to obtain price, delivery, other market information, and capabilities for planning purposes. Responses to these RFIs are not offers and cannot be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract. This RFI shall not be construed as a commitment by the Government for any purpose, nor does it restrict the Government to an ultimate acquisition approach. Respondents are solely responsible for all expenses associated with their RFI response. Respondents will not receive additional information in response to their submittal to the RFI and will not be notified of the resulting market research. Interested contractors shall submit their RFI responses electronically to Danyelle Wilcox, Contracting Officer, at Danyelle.Wilcox@fema.dhs.gov and Danielle Sweetney, Contract Specialist, at Danielle.Sweetney@fema.dhs.gov no later than 11:00 am Eastern Time (ET), August 31, 2026. Questions regarding this RFI are due no later than 11:00 am ET August 14, 2026.

description: DEPARTMENT OF VETERANS AFFAIRS Regional Procurement Office-West (RPOW) Sources Sought Notification 36C24W26Q0231 REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) / SOURCES SOUGHT FOR LEASE LOCATION The VA San Diego Healthcare System (VASDHS) is seeking one lease acquisition of approximately 19,000 Net Usable Square Feet (NUSF) for a new Dental Clinic in the city of Chula Vista, CA. This site will help with providing Dental Services to our Veterans and house the current Dental Service located in Building 11 of the Jennifer Moreno Medical Center (San Diego) in preparation for renovation of Building 11 and to eliminate the need to outsource dental care. The Government seeks to award a lease contract for 5 years firm term and 5 years soft term (up to 10 years total) due to both immediate and future known requirements. The space shall be in a quality building, constructed of sound and substantial construction, and shall be in compliance with Federal Laws & Regulations governing Federal Leases, Building and Fire codes, and the Americans with Disabilities Act. If not a new Building, the Space offered shall be in a Building that has undergone or will be completed by occupancy, modernization, or adaptive reuse for the Space with modern conveniences. Access to public transportation shall be located within the immediate vicinity of the building, but generally not to exceed a walkable one mile as determined by the Contracting Officer. Alternatively, two or more public or campus bus lines usable by Veterans shall be located within the immediate vicinity of the building, but generally not to exceed a walkable ¼ mile. Offered space must meet government requirements for fire, safety, accessibility, seismic and sustainability standards per the terms of the lease. Space offered shall not be in the 100-year floodplain. The VA is conducting market research/seeking capable sources from bondable and experienced firms that are classified and registered in www.vip.vetbiz.gov as either a Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Businesses (SDVOSB) or Veteran-Owned Small Businesses (VOSB). The NAICS Code is 531120 Lessors of Nonresidential Buildings, and the small business size standard is $30 million annual revenue. Responses to this notice will assist the VA in determining if the acquisition should be set-aside for competition restricted to SDVOSB or VOSB concerns in accordance with 38 USC Sec. 8127. Although this notice focuses on SDVOSB and VOSB, we encourage ALL small businesses and other interested parties to respond for market research purposes. Expressions for offeror shall be sent no later than 8:00 AM PDT on Monday, August 31, 2026. The VA is seeking under PL 109-461 Veterans First, a Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business or Veteran-Owned Small Business Lessor or Owner able to provide the following space: City, State Chula Vista, California Delineated Area North boundary: I-8 South Boundary: Otay River East Boundary: CA-125 West Boundary: I-5 / CA-15 / I-805 Minimum Sq. Interested offerors shall include the following: Name of Property Address Proof of Ownership Proof of Representation Pictures Space Layout Proof property is within the delineated area (see Attachment) This will be a fully-serviced lease with a term of 5 years firm and 5 years soft term (up to 10 years total) with the VA having the option to vacate the premises with a 180-day notice. description: 13 August 2026 Posted Question and Answer document 6 August 2026-Document 05D-DWG-F30001 (SAM.gov will not accept this type of document, interested vendors should email Brian Algeo, (brian.algeo.1@us.af.mil) to request the document. Special Notice: Brand Name Haworth Furniture Solicitation Number: FA8601-26-Q-0111 Notice Type: Special (RFQ) Issuing Office: AFLCMC/PZIBA Posted Date: July 28, 2026 Response Date: August 31, 2026, 11:00 AM EDT Set-Aside: N/A Classification Code (PSC): 7110 NAICS Code: 337214 Small Business Size Standard: 1,100 Employees Description: The Air Force Life Cycle Management Center (AFLCMC/PZIBA), on behalf of Department of the Air Force at Wright Patterson Air Force Base (WPAFB), intends to award a Brand Name Only, firm-fixed-price contract for Haworth Furniture. This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial products prepared in accordance with Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation Overhaul (RFO) Part 12. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation; offers are being requested and a separate written solicitation will not be issued. This solicitation incorporates provisions and clauses in effect through the RFO (effective April 17, 2026) and the Revolutionary Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation Supplement (RDFARS) as of the date of issuance. The Department of the Air Force intends to award a firm-fixed-price contract for Haworth Furniture in accordance with the attached Statement of Work (SOW), on a Lowest Price Technically Acceptable (LPTA) basis. The Schedule of Supplies, place of performance, delivery information, and the full list of applicable provisions and clauses are set forth in the attached SF 1449 and solicitation. Award is subject to the availability of funds. The requirement is for all supplies, labor, and services necessary to complete the furniture requirement of WBAFB. This is a follow-on project that requires new workstations to be physically compatible and fully interchangeable with the existing Haworth furniture. The Government's market research indicates that Haworth products utilize proprietary physical connections, and no other manufacturer produces a compatible system that can meet the Government's essential need for a single, integrated, and reconfigurable workspace. In accordance with the Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation Overhaul, (RFO) 5.101(c)(4)(vii), the justification for restricting competition is that the proprietary Haworth physical connections and design are essential to the Government's requirement, and no other brand of systems furniture can interface with the existing setup. Therefore, this acquisition is being conducted under the authority of (RFO) 6.103-1. This is a BRAND NAME ONLY requirement. Only brand name Haworth products will be accepted. "Or Equal" products will NOT be evaluated. Standardization of Haworth is required to ensure compatibility with existing systems, eliminate duplication of training costs and maintain mission continuity. In accordance with RFO 5.201(c)(3), the approved Brand Name Justification and Approval (J&A) is attached to this posting on SAM.gov. title: LS-DYNA Licenses Renewal
description: The Office of Procurement Operations (OPO) on behalf of the Office of Science and Technology (S&T) Directorate hereby issues this notice of intent to award a sole-source procurement. DHS OPO intends to solicit and award a sole source order for LS-DYNA licenses to ANSYS, Inc. 275 TECHNOLOGY DRIVE SOUTHPOINTE CANONSBURG PA 15317-9565. This notice of intent to solicit and award a sole source order under the authority of Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation Overhaul (RFO) FAR 12.102(a) �only one source available.� The relevant NAICS code is 423430 � Computer and Computer Peripheral Equipment and Software Merchant Wholesalers, with a size standard of 1,000 employees. The PSC code is H270 � EQUIPMENT AND MATERIALS TESTING. Summary of the Requirement Background DHS Science and Technology (S&T), Office of Science and Engineering (OSE), Transportation Security Laboratory (TSL) provides scientists and engineers with knowledge, experience, and expertise in all areas of contraband detection with an emphasis on explosives. The core mission of the TSL is to enhance homeland security by performing research, development, and validation of solutions to detect and mitigate the threat of explosive devices and contraband materials. The CAVM program at TSL, has accumulated a large amount of test data that has traditionally been conducted on aluminum body aircraft and aluminum aircraft panels. By using past and present live fire test data and standard properties of explosives and mechanics of materials, a Modeling and Simulation (M&S) capability facilitates the prediction of responses of various aircraft structures to internal explosive blasts under pressurized conditions to include mechanical analysis techniques such as finite element analysis (FEA) or hydrodynamic software. This has been previously achieved with the utilization of LS-DYNA licenses. LS-DYNA licenses are currently provided under Department of Homeland Security (DHS) purchase order 70RSAT25P00000012. Scope These licenses help to provide M&S capabilities that assist with the tests related to commercial passenger aircraft safety like composite aircraft testing and explosive characterization testing. To continue the blast response M&S effort without interruption, renewal of this software is crucial and time sensitive. Period of Performance: 12-month base period. DHS has determined that LS-DYNA license subscriptions can only be obtained from Ansys, Inc. A determination by the Government not to compete based upon responses to this notice is solely at the discretion of the Government. This is a notice of the intent to award a sole source contract. It is published for informational purposes only and not a request for competitive proposals. Therefore, no solicitation document exists for this requirement. Any firm believing that they can fulfill the requirement may be considered by the agency. Interested parties may identify their interest and capabilities in response to this synopsis. All questions and/or comments regarding this notice shall be addressed in writing to the Contract Specialist Marco Macherelli at Marco.Macherelli@hq.dhs.gov by August 31st, 2026 by 11:00 AM Eastern Daylight Time. Questions by phone will not be considered.

title: Behavioral Health Services
description: This solicitation amendment is issued as a combined synopsis and solicitation for commercial services under the authority of 41 U.S.C. � 3305 (Simplified procedures for small business and commercial items) and 41 U.S.C. � 1901 (Simplified acquisition procedures). Solicitation number W912J726QA0020002 amendment is issued as a request for quotation (RFQ) for Behavior Health Counseling Support ServiceBehavior Health CounselingSupport Services. This procurement is established as a 100% Women-Owned Small Business (WOSB) set-aside in accordance with the Small Business Act, specifically 15 U.S.C. � 637(m) (Women-owned small business companion program). Quotations are solicited exclusively from certified WOSB concerns eligible under the WOSB Program (including Economically Disadvantaged Women-Owned Small Business (EDWOSB) concerns) in accordance with the statutory standards of 15 U.S.C. � 637(m) and 13 CFR part 127. Quotes received from non-eligible concerns will not be considered. The Idaho National Guard J9 Service Member and Family Support have a requirement for Behavior HealthCounseling services to Service Members and their immediate family. The team shall be comprised of three(3) full-time Behavior Health Clinicians and one (1) full-time Admin Support position. This requirment has been updated to meet current organizational needs. Response Deadline: August 31, 2026, at 9:00 AM Mountain Daily Time (MDT) Primary NAICS Code: 621112 � Offices of Mental Health Practitioners (except Physicians) Size Standard: $9,000,000.00 Product Service Code (PSC): Q519 � Behavioral and Mental Health Anticipated Period of Performance: 27 Sep 2026 to 26 Sep 2027 for base period, One (1) 12-monthoption periods and one up to 6-months extension (see 52.217-9 and 52.217-8). Primary performance will be conducted at: Joint Force Headquarters, Gowen Field Military Base, Boise, ID 83705 Regional outreach travel to regional Guard offices (including Caldwell, Twin Falls, Pocatello, Idaho Falls, Lewiston, and Post Falls) may be required occasionally. INSTRUCTIONS FOR PROPOSAL SUBMISSION Quotations must be submitted electronically to the Contracting Officer, Natasha Spratt, at natasha.m.spratt2.civ@army.mil no later than August 31, 2026, at 9:00 AM MDT. All questions regarding this solicitation must be submitted via email no later than August 17, 2026. Quote Preparation: Offerors shall prepare their quotations in strict accordance with the requirements, instructions, terms, and conditions contained in this combined synopsis/solicitation, the performance work statement (PWS), and any subsequent formal amendments issued by the Government. Failure to address all requirements or incorporate any subsequent solicitation amendments may result in the quotation being determined non-compliant and excluded from further evaluation. Formatting: To ensure a structured, fair, and efficient evaluation, the offeror�s submission shall be divided into three (3) distinct sections, self-contained Portable Document Format (PDF)s compatible with standard readers. Structure: Section I: Section 1 Quote. Complete SF 1449 or the quoter's vendor commercial quote (no page limit). If providing a commercial quote without the SF 1449, the commercial quote MUST include all elements in W912J726QA0020002 clause 52.212-1 paragraph (a), and the statement requested in (a)(6), provide information pertaining to price only and provide complete pricing per SF 1449 line items schedule excluding CLIN 0005 and 1005 travel. Section II:Section 2 Capability Statement. A capability describing how the quoter intends to provide the services required in this solicitation. Stating "will comply with PWS" is not sufficient. The statement must describe the quoter's capability to meet the agency's needs as described in this solicitation. Not to exceed ten pages, Times New Roman or Arial, size 12, margins at 1-inch, single space. Section III: Section 3 Past Performance. The Government will review information obtained from Government sources including Contractor Performance Assessment Reporting System (CPARS), System of Award Responsibility/Qualifications (also known as Federal Awardee Performance and Integrity Information System (FAPIIS)), Supplier Performance Risk System (SPRS) Score, and other sources of information. Quoters shall submit a three-page past performance sheet. The past performance attachment can include Federal, non-Federal, and Private Sector. The combined experience submitted to the Government shall not exceed three pages, font Times New Roman or Arial, size 12, margins at 1-inch, single space. Information exceeding three pages will not be considered. Do NOT include Sections 1, 2 and 3 into a single document. Sections shall be submitted as separate documents. Basis of Award: Evaluation factors. The Government will award a firm-fixed-price (FFP) purchase order resulting from this solicitation to the responsible quoter who provides the lowest acceptable quote that demonstrates understanding of the requirements and conformance with the solicitation. This acquisition is being conducted strictly under simplified procedures for commercial products and commercial services. The Government is not conducting a source selection, and procedures from RFO Part 15 do not apply. To efficiently identify the lowest acceptable quote, the Government may evaluate quotes by first ranking them from lowest to highest price. The Government will then evaluate the technical and past performance factors of the lowest-priced quote. If the lowest-priced quote is determined to be acceptable, the Government may evaluate no other quotes and proceed to award. Quotes failing to meet all the terms and conditions of this solicitation, including buy terms, line-item descriptions, and attachments, will not be evaluated for award. The Government reserves the right to seek clarifications on the contents of the quote if determined necessary by the Contracting Officer. Quotes will be evaluated with the following review criteria: (i) Technical: The degree to which the quoter's proposed service meets the Government's requirements. Merely stating 'will comply with all PWS requirements' is insufficient. The Technical Proposal will be evaluated qualitatively and assigned one of the following adjectival ratings: Technical Adjectival Rating Evaluation Definition Outstanding Proposal meets all requirements and demonstrates an exceptional clinical or management approach. Contains multiple strengths that significantly benefit J9 operations, contains no weaknesses, and the risk of unsuccessful performance is extremely low. Good Proposal meets all requirements and demonstrates a thoroughly solid clinical or management approach. Contains at least one or more strengths that benefit J9 operations, contains few minor weaknesses, and the risk of unsuccessful performance is low to moderate. Acceptable Proposal meets all requirements and demonstrates an adequate clinical and management approach. Contains no significant strengths, contains some minor weaknesses, and the risk of unsuccessful performance is moderate. Marginal Proposal fails to meet one or more minor PWS requirements, contains notable weaknesses, and has a high risk of unsuccessful performance. Deficiencies are significant but correctable. Unacceptable Proposal fails to meet major requirements, contains significant deficiencies, represents an unacceptably high risk of performance failure, and cannot be made acceptable without major, complete revisions. (ii) Past Performance: The Government will consider primary Government sources for past performance such as Supplier Performance Risk System, Contractor Performance Assessment Reporting System (CPARS), Federal Awardee Performance and Integrity Information System (FAPIIS), and other sources. title: Renovate Women's Center to Conference Center
description: Mission and Installation Contracting Command (MICC) Fort Hood is issuing a SOLICITATION NOTICE for an Invitation for Bids (IFB) firm fixed price construction contract to Renovate Women�s Center to Conference Center. This consists of the interior demolition and construction to reconfigure the facility to better suit the needs of the anticipated user with administrative and conference room requirements. The work shall be located at Building 36000 located at the intersection of Wratten Drive and Shoemaker Lane Fort Hood, Texas. This acquisition is 100% Certified Women Owned Small Business Set Aside under NAICS 236220 (Size Standard $45.0 Million). The magnitude of the procurement is estimated to be between $1,000,000 and $5,000,000. The purpose of this project is to Renovate the Women�s Center to a Conference Center. This consists of the interior demolition and construction to reconfigure the facility to better suit the needs of the anticipated user with administrative and conference room requirements. The work shall be located at Building 36000 located at the intersection of Wratten Drive and Shoemaker Lane Fort Hood, Texas. Also included is miscellaneous site work to support the facility and meet code requirements. title: France – IT services: consulting, software development, Internet and support – Analyse de la vulnérabilité au changement climatique et Stratégie de résilience du Grand Port Maritime de Guyane PAD-01-26 GPM Guyane vulnérabilité PAD0126 RX
description: Réalisation d’une étude visant à analyser la vulnérabilité des infrastructures portuaires face aux effets du changement climatique, à évaluer les risques associés aux aléas climatiques actuels et futurs et proposer une stratégie de résilience. Il comprend l’identification des mesures d’adaptation appropriées, la définition d'actions pour garantir la continuité des services portuaires, et l’élaboration d’une stratégie de résilience permettant de renforcer la capacité d’adaptation, l'intégration territoriale et la pérennité des infrastructures portuaires.
